top_story: U.S.-Iran tensions have sharpened from March’s exchange of threats over the Strait of Hormuz and Iran’s power grid into a more immediate coercive phase, with Washington on 30 May signaling it is ready to restart strikes if nuclear talks fail and Tehran still facing pressure under maximal U.S. red lines. That escalation risk sits atop a wider regional strain in which any renewed clash could disrupt Gulf shipping, energy markets, and civilian infrastructure far beyond Iran itself. In parallel, the UN’s 29 May decision to blacklist Israel for conflict-related sexual violence pushed Israel to sever ties with António Guterres, deepening its confrontation with international institutions and narrowing outside avenues for scrutiny and accountability. The regional picture is one of simultaneous military brinkmanship and institutional rupture, with civilians likely to bear the costs as deterrence, diplomacy, and oversight all weaken together.
